title: Fabrication of Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold Sensors on Rubber Gloves
author: Mechael, Wu, et al.
materials: Neo for Iwata CN gravity feed dual action airbrush

steps.title: Prepare plating solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare each plating solution (Pd/Sn colloid, HCl accelerator, electroless Ni bath containing Ni²⁺ and dimethylamine borane, and gold cyanide immersion solution) using commercially available reagents according to supplier instructions; solutions may be reused until they become destabilized or depleted.

steps.title: Plasma oxidize glove surface
steps.instruction: Expose the NBR glove to plasma oxidation to generate hydrophilic functional groups on the surface and increase wettability.

steps.title: Apply latex mask (optional)
steps.instruction: Airbrush a commercial latex emulsion through a stencil mask onto the oxidized glove to create a patterned hydrophobic resist; allow the resist to dry completely before proceeding.

steps.title: Silanize surface with APTES
steps.instruction: Immerse the (masked) glove in a 3‑aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) solution so that hydrolyzed silanol groups condense with surface hydroxyls, forming an amine‑terminated NBR surface.

steps.title: Deposit Pd‑Sn catalyst
steps.instruction: Submerge the APTES‑treated glove in a palladium‑tin (Pd/Sn) colloidal catalyst suspension; the acidic pH protonates surface amines, creating a positively charged surface that electrostatically binds the negatively charged SnClx‑capped Pd colloids.

steps.title: HCl accelerator etch
steps.instruction: Treat the catalyst‑bound glove with a dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl) accelerator solution to partially etch the SnClx shell and expose the catalytic Pd core.

steps.title: Electroless nickel deposition
steps.instruction: Immerse the glove in the electroless nickel (Ni) plating bath; the exposed Pd catalyzes reduction of Ni²⁺ ions by dimethylamine borane (DMAB) to metallic Ni⁰, which then grows autocatalytically. Adjust immersion time to obtain the desired Ni film thickness.

steps.title: Remove latex mask
steps.instruction: Peel off the dried latex resist to reveal the patterned areas where metal deposition was blocked.

steps.title: Immersion gold plating
steps.instruction: Transfer the nickel‑coated glove to a gold cyanide immersion solution; Au⁺ ions galvanically displace surface Ni⁰, forming a conformal Au⁰ film while releasing Ni²⁺ into the solution.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for electroless nickel immersion gold (ENIG) plating on nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) gloves to fabricate strain sensing arrays for human motion detection. ENIG is a scalable, low temperature, solution-based gold deposition technique that encompasses two solution-based plating steps: the electroless deposition (ELD) of a nickel film followed by an immersion gold process that galvanically displaces nickel with gold from a gold cyanide salt solution (Accogli et al., 2020). ENIG is a reliable additive manufacturing method used to deposit corrosion-resistant gold layers in printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing (Accogli et al., 2020). We have previously applied this versatile process to prepare gold films on a variety of substrates such as NBR (Mechael et al., 2021), polydimethylsiloxane (Chen et al., 2019), and various textiles (Wu et al., 2018, 2020a, 2020b) for stretchable and wearable electronics. One advantage of this deposition method over physical vapor deposition (PVD) techniques is the ability to conformally deposit gold films on complex interior geometries because of the non-line-of-sight nature of solution plating. For example, our research group has applied ENIG deposition on polyester textiles to prepare conformal gold coatings that individually coat each fiber while preserving the void space between fiber bundles to maintain the wearability of the final e-textile (Wu et al., 2018). The benefit of conformal deposition also extends to the metallization of substrates with high surface roughness such as NBR gloves (Mechael et al., 2021). Here, we describe how to use ENIG to directly deposit sensing arrays on off-the-shelf NBR gloves by patterning the metal deposition on the joint locations of the hand (Mechael et al., 2021).
